recognize_zh: 紅血球聚成不規則、葡萄串狀的大團塊（agglutination），而不是像錢幣疊成一列的 rouleaux；團塊之外的紅血球形態大致正常，視野中還有一顆小淋巴球，符合冷凝集素病。
features: Irregular, three-dimensional clumps of red cells with scalloped, grape-like outlines (true agglutination), rather than linear stacks
Non-agglutinated red cells are mostly normocytic with central pallor; no definite spherocytes or schistocytes in this field
Single small mature lymphocyte with condensed chromatin and scant basophilic cytoplasm
Platelets present in normal-appearing numbers in the background
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows prominent red cell agglutination, with red cells forming irregular, branching clumps of variable size scattered throughout the field. The clumps are irregular rather than linear, distinguishing them from rouleaux. Red cells outside the clumps are largely normochromic without obvious spherocytosis in this field. A single small mature lymphocyte is present, and platelets appear adequate. Findings are consistent with red cell agglutination due to a cold agglutinin, as seen in cold agglutinin disease; correlation with warming of the sample, DAT (C3d positive) and cold agglutinin titer, and evaluation for an underlying lymphoproliferative disorder is recommended.

ddx.vs: Rouleaux form linear, coin-like stacks in thin areas that disperse with saline, whereas agglutination forms irregular grape-like clumps that disperse on warming to 37 C.
Warm AIHA typically shows spherocytes and polychromasia with IgG-positive DAT, and agglutination is usually absent or minimal.
Artifactual clumping is focal and inconsistent, while cold agglutination is diffuse, reproducible, and abolished when blood is kept and smeared at 37 C.
